## Intro

This edition covers the week of 30 November - 6 December 2026 and reports developments for commercial road freight in Germany, Azerbaijan, Estonia and Belarus, with priority for heavy, oversize and special transport. Reports: 14th Lang-Lkw Amendment in force: Type 1 extended to 2033, cab length exception to 18.41 m; Azerbaijan: Turkish carriers report height problems with oversize loads; special permit regime for out-of-gauge and heavy vehicles; Estonia to close its road border with Russia on 1 December.

## Lead reports

### 14th Lang-Lkw Amendment in force: Type 1 extended to 2033, cab length exception to 18.41 m (Germany)

The 14th Lang-Lkw Amendment Ordinance has applied since 21 November 2026. It was dated 18 November, published in the Federal Law Gazette (BGBl. I Nr. 345) on 20 November, and entered into force the following day. Type 1 (tractor unit plus semi-trailer) is extended until 2033. The existing 17.88 m overall length limit stays, but an exception up to 18.41 m now applies where the excess comes solely from an extended cab under Annex XIII of the implementing regulation. The report also refers to new routes.

**Category:** Operational development  
**Where:** Germany; Lang-Lkw network. The exact new routes are not listed in the available summary.  
**Affected vehicles:** Lang-Lkw Type 1 (articulated tractor and semi-trailer). The 18.41 m limit applies only to a two-axle tractor unit with a correspondingly extended cab. Other Lang-Lkw types are not covered by this exception.  
**When:** In force from 21 November 2026; Type 1 extended until 2033

**Impact:** Dispatchers and fleets using Lang-Lkw Type 1 get longer planning certainty and more cab space. The extended length applies only to the specific combination described. Industry report only; check the Federal Law Gazette text for the binding wording.

**Recommended action:** Check whether your combination qualifies (two-axle tractor, extended cab per Annex XIII). Verify the new route entries against the official Lang-Lkw network list and the Federal Law Gazette text before dispatching.

**Exemptions/conditions:** Not stated in the source beyond the cab-length exception for Type 1. Do not assume the exception applies to other Lang-Lkw types or standard combinations.

*Source: [Christians Blog](https://christiansblog.eu/post/bkf/bmvlangehuette/) — Industry report — not an official authority notice*

### Azerbaijan: Turkish carriers report height problems with oversize loads; special permit regime for out-of-gauge and heavy vehicles

A circular from the Denizli chamber (ARGE 2026/330, dated 19 November 2026) relays information from the Turkish Trade Ministry and the Baku trade counsellorship. Many complaints have reached the embassy and the counsellorship about problems, especially regarding height, on out-of-gauge transports to Azerbaijan by Turkish logistics firms and TIR drivers. According to the Azerbaijani land transport agency AYNA and the Road Guard Service of the State Roads Agency, out-of-gauge and heavy vehicles on public roads require a special movement permit. Fees and permitted dimension and weight parameters are set under the Azerbaijani rules.

**Category:** Operational development  
**Where:** Azerbaijan, public road network. Specific roads and the exact limits are not given in the available summary.  
**Affected vehicles:** Out-of-gauge (oversize) and heavy-tonnage vehicles travelling to or within Azerbaijan. Exact thresholds are not stated in the available excerpt.

**Impact:** Oversize loads, especially tall loads, risk problems and non-compliance at Azerbaijani controls without the correct special permit. Permit fees apply. Industry circular only; it is not an official statement of the legal conditions.

**Recommended action:** Before dispatching any oversize or heavy load to Azerbaijan, obtain the special movement permit and confirm the permitted height, width, weight and fees directly with AYNA or the Road Guard Service. Plan load height against the official limits and route.

**Exemptions/conditions:** None stated in the source.

*Source: [denib.gov.tr](https://denib.gov.tr/en/duyuru-2026-330.html)*

### Estonia to close its road border with Russia on 1 December

The Times of Central Asia, as republished by Eurasian Annals on 25 November 2026, reports that Estonia will close its road border with Russia on 1 December. Estonia cited national security reasons. Latvia is reported to be considering a similar move. The report says fewer road routes to Europe would remain for Central Asian carriers, with higher operating costs. Caspian Sea alternatives are limited by capacity, cost and delivery times.

**Category:** Operational development  
**Where:** Estonia–Russia road border. The specific crossing points are not named in the available summary.  
**Affected vehicles:** Road freight traffic across the Estonia–Russia border. Any exemptions are not stated in the available excerpt.  
**When:** From 1 December 2026, as reported

**Impact:** Carriers using the Estonia–Russia road border will need alternative routings or other transport modes, with likely longer transit times and higher costs. Latvia's possible similar step is not confirmed. Industry analysis, not an official notice.

**Recommended action:** Check current border status with the Estonian authorities before 1 December. Re-plan or re-route Baltic and Russia/CIS loads, and monitor Latvian announcements before committing transit bookings.

**Exemptions/conditions:** Not stated in the available source excerpt.

*Source: [Eurasian Annals](https://eurasianannals.gr/index.php/business-news/analyseis/central-asian-trade-routes-to-europe-face-growing-restrictions) — Industry report — regulatory/route conditions require confirmation with the competent authority*

### Belarus eases transit for EU-registered trucks in limited cases from 1 December

Per a government decree reported on 19 November 2026, from 1 December 2026 EU-registered trucks may cross Belarus without cargo reloading or trailer swapping in certain cases. These are diplomatic cargo, goods for official use by representative offices of international organizations, and radioisotope products. Empty trucks travelling to load radioisotope products or reusable packaging for their transport are also permitted. The government also updated the list of specially designated locations for reloading and trailer swapping. Restrictions on entry of EU-registered trucks and tractor units have been in place since 16 April 2022.

**Category:** Operational development  
**Where:** Belarus, transit across the territory; designated reloading and trailer-swap locations.  
**Affected vehicles:** EU-registered trucks and tractor units, only for the listed cargo categories and the related empty runs.  
**When:** From 1 December 2026

**Impact:** The easing is narrow. General EU freight carriers remain subject to the existing reloading and trailer-swap regime. Operators of the listed cargo types gain a transit option. Industry news report on a government decree.

**Recommended action:** Operators handling diplomatic, international-organization or radioisotope cargo should check the decree text and the updated list of designated locations. All others should keep planning under the existing reloading regime.

**Exemptions/conditions:** Applies only to the cargo categories listed. It is not a general lifting of the 2022 restrictions.

*Source: [Nasha Niva](https://nashaniva.com/en/409654) — Industry report — not an official authority notice*

## Operator checklist

- Germany: Check whether your combination qualifies (two-axle tractor, extended cab per Annex XIII). Verify the new route entries against the official Lang-Lkw network list and the Federal Law Gazette text before dispatching.
- Azerbaijan: Before dispatching any oversize or heavy load to Azerbaijan, obtain the special movement permit and confirm the permitted height, width, weight and fees directly with AYNA or the Road Guard Service. Plan load height against the official limits and route.
- Estonia: Check current border status with the Estonian authorities before 1 December. Re-plan or re-route Baltic and Russia/CIS loads, and monitor Latvian announcements before committing transit bookings.
- Belarus: Operators handling diplomatic, international-organization or radioisotope cargo should check the decree text and the updated list of designated locations. All others should keep planning under the existing reloading regime.

- [denib.gov.tr](https://denib.gov.tr/en/duyuru-2026-330.html)
- [Eurasian Annals](https://eurasianannals.gr/index.php/business-news/analyseis/central-asian-trade-routes-to-europe-face-growing-restrictions)
- [Nasha Niva](https://nashaniva.com/en/409654)
